newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - unwanted gas oil weak.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - unwanted gas oil weak.

text.p: Gulf middle distillate markets remain weak with cargoes struggling to find fresh homes in India, Asia and east African markets, Gulf traders on Thursday.
"There is a disappointing lack of demand for gas oil," said one trader based in the region, adding that rival barrels from the Mediterranean continued to cap Gulf prices.

One percent sulphur Gulf gas oil was talked at a 30-40 cents premium to independent price quotes though one Kuwaiti 0.5 percent cargo was said sold to a trader at 60-65 cents, up from the last deal -- an Abu Dhabi cargo -- at plus 40 cents.
Kerosene, suffering from a seasonal downturn in demand, was talked around a 25-35 cents premium, following on from the sale of an Abu Dhabi cargo at 25 cents, traders said.

Gas oil was assessed at around $24.30 a barrel fob Gulf -- 50 cents down on the week -- and kerosene at $23.30 a barrel. Some kerosene buying was noted for putting into storage in Jebel Ali, Dubai though this was barely enough to turn the market around, traders said.
Yemen was said by traders to have reissued its tender to sell 30,000 tonnes of kerosene for May 11-13 delivery while Oman had tendered to buy leaded gasoline for May delivery.

Gas oil and kerosene sellers faced few buyers and market premiums were unlikely to improve even if Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) high speed diesel buying tender for June delivery beat market expectations, they said.
IOC, which awarded 870,000 tonnes of diesel for May, is expected to award its June spot tender in the next 24 hours.
The state oil firm's tender for term supplies of diesel and superior kerosene for delivery June 1997-May 1998 has been delayed and will close on May 7, instead of April 29.
Spot tenders from Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka were also unlikely to spur a recovery in the short-term when cargoes out of Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Bahrain were unsold, traders said.
"Singapore has far too much (gas oil) on its plate. The Gulf is suffering from too many unsold barrels," another trader said.
Fuel oil markets were fundamentally stronger than middle distillates, based on stronger Asian market and an upturn in the Fujairah bunker market, traders said.
Fuel 180 sct was assessed at $90 a tonne, up $1 while Fujairah 380-cst bunkers held up at $95 a tonne.
